sections.h2: What to line up before listing in Westlake
sections.html:
Westlake is a Cuyahoga County suburb about 12 miles west of downtown Cleveland, with an estimated 33,904 residents, 1.0% under its 2020 base. City Hall sits at 27700 Hilliard Boulevard, phone 440-871-3300, open 8 am to 4 pm.

For permits and property maintenance, ask City Hall directly. For deeds and value complaints, use the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office and Board of Revision. The sections below explain what each office does.

sections.h2: Housing costs and who lives here
sections.html:
Westlake is an older suburb where most households own.

  • 73.1% of homes are occupied by their owners, and the middle value among them is $368,200.
  • Owners with a mortgage spend $2,071 a month on housing; owners without one spend $926.
  • Renters pay $1,570 a month at the midpoint.
  • 14,424 households share the city, averaging 2.29 people.
  • Half of households earn more than $112,200.
  • 25.1% of residents are 65 or older, and the median age is 47.4.

With that age profile, many Westlake sales involve owners downsizing or heirs settling an estate. The 2020 count found 15,508 housing units, 5.7% of them vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%, so few owner-occupied homes sat empty while apartments stood open more often.

Dover Village took the name Westlake in 1940 and became a city in 1957. Growth came fast, from 12,906 residents in 1960 to 27,018 in 1990 and 34,228 in 2020, so much of the housing is a few decades old.

Crocker Park, a mixed-use center built around a small-town street plan, holds 1,050,000 square feet of retail, 650 residential units and 100,000 square feet of office space. Westlake commuters average 24.4 minutes each way, which is worth mentioning to buyers who work downtown.

sections.h2: Deed transfer at the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office
sections.html:
A Westlake deed doesn't go to a city office. It goes to the county Fiscal Office, where the Transfer and Recording division holds the duties of the former auditor, recorder and engineer. The phone number is 216-443-2060.

  • Each transfer must arrive with one of two state forms: the DTE 100 value statement and receipt, or the DTE 100-EX explaining why the conveyance fee is exempt.
  • Staff can't draft your deed. The county treats that as legal work, so have the document prepared by a title company or attorney.
Where to go for common Westlake sale tasks
TaskOfficeWhat to know
Permits, building and property maintenance questionsCity of Westlake Building Department, through City Hall at 440-871-3300City Hall hours are 8 am to 4 pm
Deed transfer and recordingCuyahoga County Fiscal Office, 216-443-2060DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX accompanies each transfer
Value complaintCuyahoga County Board of Revision, 216-443-7195Complaint window opens January 1 and ends March 31

The Cuyahoga County Board of Revision decides complaints about real property valuation under Chapter 5715 of the Revised Code. The period for tax year 2026 runs January 1 to March 31, 2027. By statute the cutoff is the end of March after the tax year, or the close of first-half collection when that comes later.

The board works from the second floor at 2079 East Ninth Street, phone 216-443-7195, email BORInfo@cuyahogacounty.gov. Its site posts the state forms, a searchable list of closed and pending complaints since 2018 and guidance on evidence. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 requires a complainant to give the board all information or evidence they hold that affects the property.

Read the evidence guidance on the board's site before you file. A complainant who withholds evidence can be barred from using it on appeal.

The 2020 count found 14,618 households. Married couples headed 49.4% of them, single-person households made up 35.3%, and 16.3% were someone 65 or older living alone. Only 22.8% had children under 18. That mix suggests buyers who want less upkeep as well as families, so a tidy house with simple systems can appeal to both.

A typical owner-occupied value of $368,200 points to buyers who finance with a mortgage, which ties the timeline to their lender. A direct as-is purchase can close on a date you pick, at a price that reflects the repairs involved.

  • Get each offer on paper with the closing date, the party paying closing costs and any repair exclusions.
  • Ask any cash buyer for proof of funds first.
  • Compare the amount left after paying off a mortgage and unpaid property tax, since the headline price overstates your proceeds.

sections.h2: Questions to ask City Hall before listing
sections.html:
Rather than guess at local rules, put the same short list of questions to City Hall.

  • Is there an open permit, or one that never received a final inspection?
  • If the house is a rental, does the city require a license or registration, and does it pass to a new owner?
  • Are there any open property maintenance or zoning complaints?
  • Which sewer and water accounts need a final reading at closing?
  • Do you have the signed state disclosure form ready? Section 5302.30 of the Revised Code makes sellers of one-to-four unit homes deliver it, with exceptions for estates and some family transfers.

Record each answer with the date and the department. The title company handling the closing is likely to ask the same questions.

Once you have answers, work through the county side. Ask a title company or attorney to prepare the deed, choose the right DTE form, and confirm what the Fiscal Office needs before the closing date. A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal, but not these local and county steps.

faqs.q: By when must a Westlake value complaint be filed?
faqs.a: The end of March following the tax year. For tax year 2026 the Board of Revision lists January 1 through March 31, 2027. Call 216-443-7195 with questions.

faqs.q: Who prepares the deed for a Westlake sale?
faqs.a: A title company or attorney does. Fiscal Office staff can't draft deeds because the county treats that as legal work. Each transfer goes with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX.

faqs.q: Where do I call about Westlake permits and property maintenance?
faqs.a: City Hall at 440-871-3300, open 8 am to 4 pm. Ask about any open permit that never got a final inspection and any open maintenance or zoning complaint.

faqs.q: What does Westlake's disclosure form cover?
faqs.a: Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 makes sellers of one-to-four unit homes deliver the state form to the buyer. Estates and some family transfers are exempt.

faqs.q: How should I compare a cash offer with a listing?
faqs.a: Get each offer in writing with the closing date, who pays closing costs and any repair exclusions. Ask a cash buyer for proof of funds, and compare what you'd keep after paying off a mortgage and unpaid property tax.
